observation.visible_scene: A coastal seascape at sunset/sunrise viewed from the beach: a band of orange, yellow and teal clouds over a flat ocean horizon, a low breaking wave in the mid-distance, and a wide sheet of wet sand in the foreground that mirrors the sky's orange and cyan tones.
visible_changes: The camera framing is static across all frames: the horizon line, the cloud layout, and the position of the distant breaking-wave crest remain at the same image coordinates.

The white foam / swash edge that separates the darker water band from the reflective wet sand drifts gradually downward (toward the viewer) from the first to the last frame, i.e. the thin sheet of water advances slowly up the beach.
The orange and cyan reflections on the wet sand shimmer and shift shape as that moving water film changes, while the overall reflected color pattern stays anchored to the sky.
The distant breaking-wave crest shows only minor undulation, with no large-scale translation or collapse within the excerpt.
The clouds themselves show no perceptible drift over the ~2.7 s segment.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the advancing swash later recedes or a new wave arrives (the segment ends mid-motion).
The full wave period, the cause of the swell, and events before t=0 or after the last frame.
The exact location, time of day, and tide state.
uncertain_details: The downward drift of the foam line could be a single slow run-up or the tail of a receding wave; the frames support a gradual positional change but not a definitive wave phase.
Any very small camera movement cannot be fully excluded, though the fixed horizon and cloud positions indicate the shot is essentially locked.
Subtle changes in the distant wave texture are too slight to confirm as motion rather than compression artifacts.
